Consult Summary:
- 28-year-old woman with acute onset left posterior throbbing headache starting yesterday mid-morning, severe (8/10), not responsive to ibuprofen; advised stronger analgesia, rest, hydration, and to recontact if worsening or new symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - New-onset headache localized to left posterior head/occiput, described as intense, throbbing.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset: began yesterday mid-morning.
  - Course: built up gradually over a short period when it started; persistent since onset; severity reported as 8/10.
  - Patient reports this is unusual; has not had headaches like this previously ("not really").
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No clear exacerbating or relieving factors reported; no change with lying down, standing, bending, coughing, or sneezing.
  - Took ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday without significant effect.
  - Advised to try a stronger analgesic (unnamed) regularly with food; paracetamol may be used in combination.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Denies nausea, vomiting.
  - Denies blurred vision, eye pain, photopsia/visual auras, sensitivity to light.
  - Denies focal neurological symptoms (no tingling, numbness, weakness).
  - Denies fever, shivering, sweating.
  - Denies rash.
  - Denies neck stiffness (patient did not report neck stiffness).
  - Appetite and fluid intake reported as normal.
- Functional impact:
  - Has not missed work but is finding it very difficult to perform work and normal activities.
- Other relevant negatives:
  - No prior history of chronic headaches or migraine (patient states "not really").
  - No reported stomach problems or asthma.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- No regular prescription medications reported.
- Medications mentioned:
  - Ibuprofen (Nurofen) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - No allergies reported.

Social History:
- Age: 28 years.
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: designer.
- Tobacco: denies smoking.
- Alcohol: denies regular alcohol use.
- Recreational drugs: denies use.
- No financial or other lifestyle factors reported.

Family History:
- Mother: hypertension and history of migraines.
- No other family history mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none documented in transcript.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or tests were performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute left posterior (occipital) throbbing headache, severe (8/10), new onset (since yesterday), not responsive to initial ibuprofen.
  - Assessment: acute primary headache symptoms per history; first episode of this type reported. (Definitive diagnosis not stated in transcript.)
  - Plan:
    - Trial of a "slightly stronger" analgesic instead of ibuprofen — prescribed/recommended medication name, dose, route, and frequency not documented in transcript.
    - Paracetamol may be taken in combination (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Take analgesia regularly with food.
    - Rest and maintain good hydration.
    - Advise to seek reassessment if pain worsens or if new symptoms occur (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness).
    - If recurrent episodes of the same type or if not improving within 24–48 hours after trying recommended medication from the pharmacy, contact the service for further evaluation and planning.
    - Follow-up: patient advised to call back if not settling in next day or two after trying recommended medication.

- Issue 2: Functional impairment due to headache (difficulty performing work tasks).
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic management as above; re-evaluation if persistent impact on function.

- Issue 3: Family history of migraine (mother) — noted but no prior personal history of migraine aside from current episode.
  - Plan:
    - Consider further evaluation if headaches recur or meet criteria for migraine on follow-up.

General plan items:
- Provide symptomatic analgesia as above via pharmacy (specific prescription details not documented).
- Safety-netting education provided regarding red-flag symptoms and timeframe for recontact.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) were not recorded.
  - Formal neurological and physical examination findings not documented.
  - Specific analgesic name/dose/route/frequency recommended by clinician not documented in transcript.
  - Pregnancy status or last menstrual period not documented (relevant for medication safety in women of childbearing age).
  - Medication reconciliation beyond the single reported ibuprofen dose not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Dialogue clear and audible; clinically relevant information conveyed directly; minimal background noise.
